title: The Kubernetes Controller Manager must create unique service accounts for each work payload.
criterion: V-242381/SV-242381r1043176_rule [CAT I] The Kubernetes Controller Manager must create unique service accounts for each work payload. - Check: Change to the /etc/kubernetes/manifests directory on the Kubernetes Control Plane. Run the command: grep -i use-service-account-credentials * If the setting "--use-service-account-credentials" is not configured in the Kubernetes Controller Manager manifest... - Fix: Edit the Kubernetes Controller Manager manifest file in the /etc/kubernetes/manifests directory on the Kubernetes Control Plane. Set the value of "--use-service-account-credentials" to "true".

criterion: V-242383/SV-242383r1137641_rule [CAT I] User-managed resources must be created in dedicated namespaces. - Check: To view the available namespaces, run the command: kubectl get namespaces The default namespaces to be validated are default, kube-public, and kube-node-lease if it is created. For the default namespace, execute the commands: kubectl config set-context... - Fix: Move any user-managed resources from the default, kube-public, and kube-node-lease namespaces to user namespaces.

title: Sensitive information must be stored using Kubernetes Secrets or an external Secret store provider.
criterion: V-274883/SV-274883r1107239_rule [CAT I] Sensitive information must be stored using Kubernetes Secrets or an external Secret store provider. - Check: On the Kubernetes Master node, run the following command: kubectl get all,cm -A -o yaml Manually review the output for sensitive information. If any sensitive information is found, this is a finding. - Fix: Any sensitive information found must be stored in an approved external Secret store provider or use Kubernetes Secrets (attached on an as-needed basis to pods).
